title: Perfect local lifting of a lisse residue reduction
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-pc-scheme]. Let $(A,I)$ be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$. Use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and inverse limits of sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Suppose $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_X}(A/I)_X$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is etale locally on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] isomorphic to the constant complex of a perfect $A/I$-complex: there is an etale covering on each member of which $M_1$ is isomorphic, after pullback to the pro-etale site, to a bounded complex of constant sheaves of finite projective $A/I$-modules [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_j\to X\}$ and perfect $A$-complexes $P_j$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], meaning bounded complexes of finite projective $A$-modules, with $M|_{U_j}\simeq B_X|_{U_j}\otimes_A^L P_j$. Here tensor with $A$ means tensor with its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and restriction is to the corresponding localized site. No stratification or compatible etale witnesses are asserted in this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 09C6, lemma-connected-adic-lisse, applied on connected open components of a Noetherian scheme; coefficient change by lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence. Also literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.6.8 and Proposition 6.6.11, local lifting ingredient.

proof.text: Work locally on a member of the given etale residue-trivializing cover, then on each connected clopen component of a Noetherian affine open neighborhood. Etale maps are locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type; the locally-Noetherian finite-type lemma makes their sources locally Noetherian. Such neighborhoods cover: a Noetherian affine has finitely many irreducible components (otherwise recursively split a closed counterexample, contradicting the descending chain condition); grouping these finitely many components by chains of nonempty intersections gives its finitely many clopen connected components. Discard empty members. On this neighborhood choose one bounded finite-projective residue model $F$ with terms in $[a,b]$. Use the localization lemma as a canonical equivalence of sites after choosing small skeleta, rather than a literal isomorphism of those skeleta. Compute restriction on the equivalent concrete localized site. Slice restriction preserves kernels and products by the section formula $F|_U(V\to U)=F(V)$. It preserves epimorphisms because any section over $V$ lifts on a covering of $V$, and that same covering, with its structural maps to $U$, is a covering in the slice. Thus restriction is exact; it also preserves constant sheaves and their inverse limits. By exact countable products and the Roos triangle it commutes with the derived limits of strict towers. It therefore preserves the quotient-completion unit in the constant-completion equivalence. Hence the restricted $M$ remains complete and is the derived limit of its quotient tower. Use the coefficient datum's normalization maps and cocycles throughout; no independently chosen transitions are substituted.

source.place: Tag 09C6, connected-local reduction; Tag 099M; explicit slice and component arguments

proof.text: Write $N=\operatorname{Res}_{\underline A}M$. The constant-completion equivalence identifies $N\otimes_A^L A/I^n$ with $M_n$, compatibly with transitions. Prove by induction that every $M_n$ is supported in $[a,b]$ and has pro-etale locally constant finite cohomology. The base is the given perfect constant model $F$ for $M_1$. Put $J_n=I^n/I^{n+1}$, a finite $A/I$-module because it is a subset of the finite ring $A/I^{n+1}$. Tensor the exact constant sequence $0\to J_n\to A/I^{n+1}\to A/I^n\to0$ with $N$ to get a triangle whose outer terms are $M_1\otimes^L_{A/I}\underline{J_n}$ and $M_n$. Exactness of this constant sequence follows by taking the exact finite etale constant sequence and applying the exact comparison inverse image. The first term is the constant bounded complex $F\otimes_{A/I}J_n$, so has finite cohomology and no terms outside $[a,b]$. Derived associativity here is the balancing map $(p\otimes c)\otimes j\mapsto p\otimes cj$ on K-flat resolutions; the same computation identifies the kernel term. Tensoring a K-flat representative preserves the quasi-isomorphism from the cone of the first coefficient map to the last coefficient object, and commutes with cones, giving precisely this triangle. Regard all three terms as complexes of $A/I^{n+1}$-module sheaves, with the outer terms acted on through their quotient rings. Their finite locally constant underlying module sheaves remain finite locally constant over $A/I^{n+1}$. This finite ring is Noetherian, so the cited Serre theorem applies over that common ring. The long exact cohomology sequence then gives the induction step, including the same bounds $[a,b]$. This proves the finite-level properties rather than adding them as hypotheses; no boundedness of $N$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 094I, ideal-power filtration proof, strengthened here using the given perfect residue model

proof.text: The preceding locally constant finite sheaves are intrinsically constructible using the one-stratum partition of the nonempty connected neighborhood $Y$: take $N=1$, $Y_1=Y$ with its given scheme structure, and $i_1=\operatorname{id}_Y$. The whole space is locally closed and constructible (it is the intersection of itself as an open and a closed subset; its constructible expression uses the retrocompact opens $Y$ and $\varnothing$). For $\Lambda=A/I^n$, the canonical identification $i_1^{-1}\Lambda_Y=\Lambda_Y$ is the identity, so the module inverse image $i_1^*$ is the identity on coefficient actions and sheaves. The local finite-module models from step 2 give locally constant restrictions and finite module stalks, since a stalk of such a model is that finite module. Thus every clause of the current global finite-partition definition is satisfied, without replacing it by the affine-local Stacks convention. Finite-ring constructible derived origin therefore supplies bounded etale complexes $L_n$ and isomorphisms $\alpha_n:\nu^*L_n\simeq M_n$. The residue model is already etale, so bounded-below full faithfulness identifies $L_1$ with its given constant perfect model. Pullback commutes with derived tensor. Thus $L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n$ pulls back to $M_n$. This source is bounded: exactness of $\nu^*$ identifies its cohomology with that of $M_n$, and the sheaf unit in finite-level comparison reflects zero cohomology sheaves. Write $\rho_n:M_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n\simeq M_n$ for the datum's normalization. Full faithfulness now uniquely lifts $\alpha_n^{-1}\rho_n(\alpha_{n+1}\otimes^L A/I^n)$ to an isomorphism $\beta_n$ from that source to $L_n$. Its inverse also lifts, and faithfulness proves the quotient cocycles. Finally apply nilpotent-reduction lissity on the etale site with $B=A/I^n$, $J=I/I^n$, and $K=L_n$. Its bounded-above hypothesis holds by the established bound. Its first reduction is $L_1$ by these normalization maps (the identical reflection argument applies for reduction to level 1). Hence all cohomology sheaves of $L_n$ are finite locally constant on the etale site.

source.place: Tag 09C6, passage to etale $L_n$; Tag 094I; explicit reflection and full-faithfulness construction

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ of the nonempty connected neighborhood and set $E_n=(L_n)_{\bar x}$, taking the exact stalk functor termwise on complexes. Apply that same functor to every $\beta_n$ to get algebraic normalization isomorphisms $E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n\simeq E_n$. Stalks commute with tensor and preserve its associativity and coefficient maps: for derived tensor use the ringed-topos derived tensor pullback theorem for the point morphism. Its K-flat pullback computation and exactness of stalks identify this derived pullback with the termwise stalk. Put $t_n:E_{n+1}\to E_n$ equal to the scalar-extension unit $E_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}(E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A/I^{n+1}}A/I^n)$ followed by the restriction of the stalk of $\beta_n$. This is a map in $D(A/I^{n+1})$ whose adjoint reduction map is exactly that stalk normalization isomorphism. The unit is represented on a K-flat resolution by $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, so the iterated units and balancing maps reproduce the quotient cocycles already proved in step 3. Thus these specified $t_n$, not arbitrary maps between local models, give the algebraic tower required by the reconstruction lemma; restrict them further to $D(A)$ when forming its derived limit. Each $E_n$ is bounded with finite cohomology, and has a bounded finite-module representative: take the stalk of any constant finite-module local model supplied by finite-ring local constancy. The connected clause of finite-ring derived local constancy says $L_n$ is etale locally the constant complex $E_n$, and $E_1$ is perfect by the chosen residue model and the constant-sheaf stalk identity. Apply the algebraic perfect inverse-limit reconstruction lemma to this tower. It gives a perfect $P\in D(A)$ and compatible isomorphisms $P\otimes_A^L A/I^n\simeq E_n$; choose a bounded finite-projective representative for $P$.

proof.text: For each $n$, finite-ring derived local constancy identifies the sheaf of isomorphisms $\operatorname{Isom}(\underline{E_n},L_n)$ as finite locally constant. Its stalks are nonempty because the chosen neighborhood $Y$ is connected and $L_n$ is locally the constant stalk model $E_n$. Supply the algebraic normalization maps of step 4 and etale normalization maps of step 3, with their cocycles, to compatible finite derived trivialization. It gives one pro-etale covering and compatible isomorphisms $\underline{E_n}|_U\simeq\nu^*L_n|_U$. Compose with $\alpha_n$ and the reductions of $P$ to identify $\underline{P\otimes_A^L A/I^n}|_U\simeq M_n|_U$, compatibly for all $n$. The nonempty finite isomorphism sheaves, not an unproved simultaneous choice of independent trivializations, are the input to this step.

source.place: Tag 09C6, final compatible-isomorphism argument; Tag 09BV, finite-isomorphism-sheaf adaptation

proof.text: It remains to identify the derived limit of the left tower, including after restriction to $U$. For each finite-projective term $P^q$, choose an idempotent $e$ on $A^r$ with image $P^q$. Its finite reductions are the images of the same idempotent modulo $I^n$. Their constant sheaves have sectionwise surjective transition maps by constant-module section properties. For any sectionwise surjective tower, $1-s$ on the product is sectionwise surjective: given $(y_n)$ choose $x_1$ and recursively lift $x_n-y_n$ to $x_{n+1}$. Its kernel is the ordinary inverse limit. The latter for the summand in question is $e B_U^r=B_U\otimes_A P^q$, since finite sums and idempotents commute with inverse limits. The Roos triangle and exact countable products therefore identify $R\lim_n\underline{P\otimes_A A/I^n}|_U$ with the bounded complex $B_U\otimes_A P$. Flatness of $B_U$ over constant $A$ identifies this with $B_U\otimes_A^L P$. On the right, slice restriction preserves products and is exact as in step 1; applying it to the quotient-completion Roos triangle gives $R\lim_n M_n|_U\simeq M|_U$. A compatible isomorphism of towers induces an isomorphism of their products commuting with $1-s$, and hence an isomorphism of the fibers (complete the square to a morphism of distinguished triangles; its cohomology sequence shows the fiber map is an isomorphism). Applying this to step 5 proves the claimed local realization. Assemble the covers of the connected affine neighborhoods. For $X$ empty use the empty covering.
